references.text: Caleb and Joshua encourage the people again to trust in the Lord and not fear the Canaanites, reaffirming their confidence that they can take possession of the land.
The Lord promises that Caleb will enter the land because of his faithful spirit and wholehearted following.
Caleb is mentioned as one who followed the Lord wholeheartedly, in contrast to the other spies.
Moses reminds the people that Caleb received the promise of the land because he followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
Caleb receives Hebron as an inheritance because he followed the Lord wholeheartedly, fulfilling the promise given on account of his faith.
Caleb takes Hebron and drives out the three sons of Anak, showing that he truly could take possession of the land as he had said.
David expresses similar trust in the Lord amid danger and opposition from enemies.
The Lord encourages His people not to fear because He is with them and will strengthen them.
Hebrews refers to the unbelief of the Israelites that prevented them from entering the land, in contrast to Caleb's faith.
The warning against losing the promise of rest due to unbelief, where Caleb's faith stands as a positive example.
Paul expresses confidence that he can do all things through Christ who strengthens him, a similar declaration of faith like Caleb's.
